title: Cullet
description: Designed in glass. A real-time material studio whose hero is a slab of frosted quartz cut into shards that tilt, lift and carry selectable text; scrolling cleaves it apart into a pinned glossary of five optical terms, a live WebGL glass sampler with a glTF readout, and a library of six cuts.
stack: Next.js 16 · React 19 · three.js WebGL · Scroll-Driven CSS · Lenis

sizes.name: Size / Fc Lift
sizes.value: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--fc-white) 90%, transparent) inset, 0 18px 40px -18px color-mix(in oklab, var(--fc-ink) 22%, transparent), 0 2px 6px color-mix(in oklab, var(--fc-ink) 5%, transparent)

sections.title: Header
sections.summary: (fixed glass bar): lockup, Terms · Studio · Materials · Pricing with a cobalt indicator that slides (transform only) to the current section, "Open studio". It arrives once the slab has cleaved, tucks away on scroll-down and returns on scroll-up, and has a page-progress hairline. On phones: a menu sheet that opens with a clip-path circle from the toggle, staggers its links, traps focus, closes on Escape and gives focus back.

sections.title: Terms
sections.summary: (`#terms`, Chapter 01, held for 5 × 78svh on ≥960px): a rail of five numbered terms (Iridescence, Index of refraction, Dispersion, Transmission, Roughness) with a sliding glass pill; one glass figure at a time with an SVG ray diagram (thin film, Snell, prism with a spectral fan, a frosted slab scattering, micro-shards with narrow and wide cones), a readout chip, `01 / 05`, the term and its definition. Each step wipes the figure in on a diagonal and draws its rays in order. The rail jumps to a step. Elsewhere it is five stacked cards.

sections.title: Studio
sections.summary: (`#sampler`, Chapter 02, "Turn the dials. Watch the light."): a white sheet that slides over the held terms. A 4:3 stage (WebGL near the viewport on desktop, on tap on touch) with a 10-face lathe gem in transmissive `MeshPhysicalMaterial` in front of a striped studio card, turning slowly and dragged with inertia, with a HUD ("Live · WebGL" and the measured frame time). Six preset chips; five range dials (IOR 1–2.4, dispersion 0–1, roughness 0–1, thickness 0.1–4 cm, iridescence 0–1); the Abbe number; and a glTF readout (`KHR_materials_ior/_dispersion/_transmission/_volume/_iridescence`) whose changed line flashes, with "Copy JSON". Before WebGL, an SVG poster answers every dial: the fan bends `34°·(ior−1)`, spreads `46°·d·(ior−1)`, blurs with roughness, and a film tint follows iridescence.
sections.customCodeReason: Contains interactive 3D/WebGL, procedural canvas, or pinned scroll-scrubbed stage requiring an HtmlEmbed + page footer script.

sections.title: Workflow
sections.summary: (`#workflow`, Chapter 03, "Cut. Preview. Ship."): three steps joined by a drawn cobalt line, each with a working surface: a layer stack, three renderer tiles with ms readouts, and a code snippet.

sections.title: Materials
sections.summary: (`#materials`, Chapter 04, "Six cuts to start from."): a white sheet whose top edge is a cut line that levels out as it enters. Six cards (Crown silica CU-152, Dense flint CU-172, Frosted quartz CU-154, Borosilicate CU-147, Sapphire CU-177, Opal film CU-145) with palette-only CSS glass swatches, IOR / Abbe / roughness, a use line, and "Open in studio", which loads the preset into the sampler and travels there.

sections.title: Proof
sections.summary: (`#proof`, Chapter 05, "Glass that fits in a frame."): four count-up stats with drawn rules, a marquee of renderers that read the export, three studio notes.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: (`#pricing`, Chapter 06, "Pay for the seat, not the render."): a monthly/yearly radio switch with a sliding pill; three cuts; prices roll in on change.

sections.title: Open
sections.summary: (`#open`, Chapter 07, ink): "Your first glass is ten minutes away." with a seat form: work email, a role chip group, team size. Rules in `forms/request.ts` (tested). Invalid fields shake once, messages slide down, and focus goes to the first error. Submit shows "Cutting your seat…", then the form cleaves away and a glass shard settles with an emerald tick: "Your seat is cut." with a stable seat number and a starter material. No network request.

sections.title: Footer
sections.summary: lockup, index, a giant wordmark with a cobalt cut through it, "© 2026 Cullet Lab · a fictional brand for a landing-page template", "Back to the slab ↑".
